The State of the Coast Report

Overview

The area under consideration is located between the coordinates (106.76033, -6.154209) and (106.941261, -6.043602). This region lies in the northern part of Jakarta, Indonesia, near the Java Sea. Jakarta, the capital city of Indonesia, is the closest major city to this area. The coordinates span a section of the coastline that is part of the Jakarta metropolitan area, which is one of the most densely populated urban regions in the world. This coastal area is crucial for the local economy and infrastructure, given its proximity to the city and its role in supporting various economic activities. The coastal region in this area exhibits a mix of accretion and erosion under future climate scenarios. Under the RCP4.5 scenario, coastal change rates range from extreme erosion (-14.72 m/yr) to extreme accretion (20.01 m/yr), with notable intense erosion observed at several locations (-1.91 to -2.29 m/yr). The RCP8.5 scenario shows a similar pattern but with slightly more severe erosion rates, reaching up to -2.69 m/yr. Key changes between the two scenarios include a shift from intense erosion to severe erosion in some areas and a decrease in accretion rates. For instance, accretion rates of 7.65 m/yr under RCP4.5 decrease to 7.17 m/yr under RCP8.5. Additionally, extreme accretion rates of 20.01 m/yr under RCP4.5 slightly reduce to 19.59 m/yr under RCP8.5. Non-realistic values exceeding 100 m/yr were excluded from the analysis. The coastal change rates indicate a trend towards increased erosion under the RCP8.5 scenario, suggesting that more aggressive climate change impacts could exacerbate coastal erosion in the future. The sediment composition of the coastline is predominantly sandy, with sand making up 76.6% of the shoreline and mud accounting for 23.4%. There are no coastal cliffs, vegetated areas, or other materials present. The population distribution along the coast is varied, with significant concentrations at certain points, such as (106.82, -6.13) and (106.81, -6.13), each having a population of 81,806. Conversely, some locations, such as (106.9, -6.08) and (106.91, -6.08), have no population. Sea level rise projections indicate a consistent increase across all scenarios from 2031 to 2151, with the high-end scenario showing a rise from 0.097 mm in 2031 to 2.110 mm in 2151. The SSP126 scenario shows a more moderate increase from 0.087 mm to 0.730 mm, while the SSP245 scenario indicates a rise from 0.087 mm to 0.945 mm. The SSP585 scenario projects an increase from 0.093 mm to 1.368 mm. These trends highlight a significant and continuous rise in sea levels, with the high-end and SSP585 scenarios showing the most substantial increases.
